subproblem.title: Exterior derivative of a form that agrees with a smooth pull-back on an open set: d(G^#ω) = G^#(dω) locally
subproblem.statement: Let P, Q, j ∈ ℕ, let G : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be C^∞, ω : ℝ^Q → Λ^j(ℝ^Q) a C^∞ j-form (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j with ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ω), θ : ℝ^P → Λ^j(ℝ^P) any j-form, and N ⊆ ℝ^P an open set with θ(x) = ω(G(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G x) for every x ∈ N. Then for every x ∈ N, (dθ)(x) = (dω)(G(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G x), where d = exteriorDerivative (SimonGMT's abbreviation of Mathlib's extDeriv).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q j : ℕ) (G : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) j) (θ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) j) (N : Set (Eucl P)), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) G → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ω → IsOpen N → (∀ x ∈ N, θ x = (ω (G x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G x)) → ∀ x ∈ N, exteriorDerivative θ x = ((exteriorDerivative ω) (G x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: (d and pull-back) in Part 0 of the supplied proof of dph_smooth_homotopy (Simon 2.5: exterior differentiation commutes with pull-back), localized to the open set on which θ agrees with the pull-back. No sibling is used; the inputs are Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq and extDeriv_pullback (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/DifferentialForm/Basic.lean).

Notation: exteriorDerivative (SimonGMT Chapter06/Forms.lean) is an abbreviation of Mathlib's extDeriv. p(y) := ω(G(y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G y) is the pull-back G^#ω. C^∞ means ContDiff of order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) = ∞.

1. Fix x ∈ N. Since N is open, N ∈ 𝓝 x (IsOpen.mem_nhds), and θ(y) = p(y) for every y ∈ N; hence θ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] p (Filter.eventually_of_mem).
2. (Locality of d.) The exterior derivative at a point depends only on the germ of the form there: Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq gives extDeriv θ x = extDeriv p x.
3. (d commutes with pull-back.) Apply Mathlib's extDeriv_pullback with smoothness order r := ∞. Its hypotheses: (a) ω is differentiable at G(x), since ω is C^∞ (ContDiff.differentiable, as 1 ≤ ∞); (b) G is C^∞ at x (ContDiff.contDiffAt); (c) minSmoothness ℝ 2 ≤ ∞ (over ℝ, minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2; closed by simp). It yields extDeriv p x = (extDeriv ω (G x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G x).
4. Steps 2 and 3 give exteriorDerivative θ x = (exteriorDerivative ω (G x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G x). As x ∈ N was arbitrary, the claim holds. ∎
proof_key_steps: For x ∈ N, θ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] G^#ω because N is open.
extDeriv_pullback (ω and G C^∞, minSmoothness ℝ 2 ≤ ∞): d(G^#ω)(x) = (dω)(G x)∘DG(x).

audit.reason: Openness supplies germ equality, and the pinned exterior-derivative locality and pullback theorems apply with the stated smoothness. Global smoothness of θ is unnecessary. The exact proposition is proved without sibling or parent reliance.

subproblem.title: Interior-product and pull-back bound |γ(w, T·, …, T·)| ≤ √(k+1)·|w|·‖T‖^k·|γ| (fact (F8))
subproblem.statement: Let m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, let γ be a (k+1)-covector on ℝ^{m′} (γ : Covector (Eucl m′) (k+1)), w ∈ ℝ^{m′}, T : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} a continuous linear map, a ∈ ℝ, and let β be a k-covector on ℝ^m with β(v) = a·γ(Fin.cons w (i ↦ T(v_i))) for every v : Fin k → ℝ^m. Then |β| ≤ |a|·√(k+1)·‖w‖·‖T‖^k·|γ|. Here |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm, the Euclidean norm of the coefficients α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}) over strictly increasing index tuples I (e = standard basis, EuclideanSpace.basisFun), ‖w‖ is the Euclidean norm and ‖T‖ the operator norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m m' k : ℕ) (γ : Covector (Eucl m') (k + 1)) (w : Eucl m') (T : Eucl m →L[ℝ] Eucl m') (a : ℝ) (β : Covector (Eucl m) k), (∀ v : Fin k → Eucl m, β v = a * γ (Fin.cons w (fun i => T (v i)))) → covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ |a| * Real.sqrt ((k : ℝ) + 1) * ‖w‖ * ‖T‖ ^ k * covectorEuclideanNorm γ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: (F8) in Part 2 of the supplied proof of dph_smooth_homotopy, with (F7) taken from the accepted sibling pullback_norm. The supplied proof bounds the contraction γ_w := γ(w, ·) by counting coefficients, which gives the constant √(m′^k)·√m′ and needs that every value γ(e_i, e_J) is ± a coefficient of γ. Here that step is replaced by Cauchy–Schwarz together with the accepted all-tuples identity tuple_sum_factorial. This avoids sorting index tuples and gives the constant √(k+1); the sibling affine_estimate only needs some constant depending on (m′, k). Siblings used: pullback_norm (iwl_sp_covectorEuclideanNorm_pullback_le) and tuple_sum_factorial (iwl_sp_pn_sum_sq_tuples_eq_factorial_mul).

Notation: for an n-covector α on ℝ^p, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin p strictly increasing} α(e∘I)²), where e_b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin p) ℝ b and e∘I := (i ↦ e_{I(i)}). Below e_b is the standard basis of ℝ^{m′}, and w_b is the b-th coordinate of w.

1. (The contraction.) Let γ_w := γ.curryLeft w (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft), a k-covector on ℝ^{m′} with γ_w(u) = γ(Matrix.vecCons w u) = γ(Fin.cons w u) for every u : Fin k → ℝ^{m′} (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply; Matrix.vecCons is Fin.cons). Then β = a • (γ_w.compContinuousLinearMap T), because at every v both sides equal a·γ(Fin.cons w (i ↦ T(v_i))).
2. (Homogeneity.) For every n-covector α on ℝ^p and c ∈ ℝ, |c•α| = |c|·|α|: each term of the defining sum is multiplied by c², so |c•α| = √(c²·S) = √(c²)·√S = |c|·|α| (Real.sqrt_mul with c² ≥ 0, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs), where S is the defining sum of α. By step 1, |β| = |a|·|γ_w.compContinuousLinearMap T|.
3. (Pull-back.) pullback_norm with P := m, Q := m′, j := k, L := T and α := γ_w gives |γ_w.compContinuousLinearMap T| ≤ ‖T‖^k·|γ_w|.
4. (Expansion in the first slot.) w = Σ_b w_b·e_b (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr for EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose coordinates are the w_b). Since γ.curryLeft is linear, γ_w = Σ_b w_b • γ.curryLeft(e_b), so γ_w(u) = Σ_b w_b·γ(Fin.cons e_b u) for every u.
5. (Cauchy–Schwarz.) Fix J : Fin k → Fin m′. Then Fin.cons e_b (e∘J) = e∘(Fin.cons b J) (compare the entry 0 and the entries i+1, Fin.cases). By step 4 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for finite sums (Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq):
   γ_w(e∘J)² = (Σ_b w_b·γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J)))² ≤ (Σ_b w_b²)·Σ_b γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J))² = ‖w‖²·Σ_b γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J))²,
   using ‖w‖² = Σ_b w_b² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq).
6. (Reindexing.) The map (b, J) ↦ Fin.cons b J is a bijection Fin m′ × (Fin k → Fin m′) → (Fin (k+1) → Fin m′) (Fin.consEquiv). Hence Σ_J Σ_b γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J))² = Σ_{I : Fin (k+1) → Fin m′} γ(e∘I)² (exchange the finite sums with Finset.sum_comm, then Fintype.sum_prod_type' and Equiv.sum_comp).
7. (All-tuples identity.) tuple_sum_factorial (with m := m′) gives Σ_{J : Fin k → Fin m′} γ_w(e∘J)² = k!·|γ_w|² and Σ_{I : Fin (k+1) → Fin m′} γ(e∘I)² = (k+1)!·|γ|². Summing step 5 over all J and using step 6: k!·|γ_w|² ≤ ‖w‖²·(k+1)!·|γ|².
8. (Bound for γ_w.) Since (k+1)! = (k+1)·k! (Nat.factorial_succ) and k! > 0, step 7 gives |γ_w|² ≤ (k+1)·‖w‖²·|γ|² = (√(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ|)² (Real.sq_sqrt). Both |γ_w| and √(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ| are ≥ 0, hence |γ_w| ≤ √(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ| (pow_le_pow_iff_left₀).
9. (Conclusion.) By steps 2, 3 and 8: |β| = |a|·|γ_w.compContinuousLinearMap T| ≤ |a|·‖T‖^k·|γ_w| ≤ |a|·‖T‖^k·√(k+1)·‖w‖·|γ| = |a|·√(k+1)·‖w‖·‖T‖^k·|γ|. No restriction on m, m′, k is used: for k = 0 there is exactly one tuple J and 0! = 1; for m′ = 0 we have w = 0 and all sums over Fin 0 are empty, so both sides vanish. ∎
proof_key_steps: β = a•(γ_w∘T) with γ_w := γ.curryLeft w; homogeneity |a•α| = |a||α| and pullback_norm give |β| ≤ |a|·‖T‖^k·|γ_w|.
γ_w(e∘J) = Σ_b w_b·γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J)), so Cauchy–Schwarz gives γ_w(e∘J)² ≤ ‖w‖²·Σ_b γ(e∘(Fin.cons b J))².
Summing over J, reindexing by Fin.consEquiv and applying the all-tuples identity: k!|γ_w|² ≤ ‖w‖²(k+1)!|γ|², hence |γ_w| ≤ √(k+1)‖w‖|γ|.

audit.reason: Scalar homogeneity, contraction, Cauchy–Schwarz, tuple reindexing and positive-factorial cancellation establish the stated √(k+1) bound. Pullback_norm finishes the estimate. Zero-degree and zero-dimensional cases are covered; both dependencies are non-circular.

subproblem.title: Locality of interval products: Z(η) = Z(η′) when η = η′ near [0,1] × spt X
subproblem.statement: Let m, q ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z). Let η, η′ ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and let N ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} be an open set with cyl(spt X) ⊆ N and η(y) = η′(y) for every y ∈ N. Then Z(η) = Z(η′). (No finiteness of M(X) is assumed.) Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p). For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1] ∧ tl(y) ∈ A}. D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ. For X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^q(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral).

Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p). For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1] ∧ tl(y) ∈ A}. For X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^q(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral). 1. (Coordinate identities.) For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m: t(cons(s, x)) = s and tl(cons(s, x)) = x. Indeed EuclideanSpace.equiv applied to (EuclideanSpace.equiv).symm f returns f (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply); then (Fin.cons s g) 0 = s (Fin.cons_zero) and Fin.tail (Fin.cons s g) = g (Fin.tail_cons); finally (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x) = x (ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply). 2. (Slice families.) Apply slice_forms (with P := m and m := q) to η and to η′. 4. (The integrands agree on [0,1].) Fix s ∈ [0,1].
   (a) j_s is continuous: x ↦ Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x) is continuous (a constant first entry and a continuous linear map; Continuous.finCons), and (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm is a continuous linear equivalence. Hence N_s := j_s⁻¹(N) is open.
   (b) spt X ⊆ N_s: for x ∈ spt X, cons(s, x) ∈ cyl(spt X) ⊆ N by step 1 and the hypothesis cyl(spt X) ⊆ N.
   (c) For x ∈ N_s the point y := cons(s, x) lies in N, so η(y) = η′(y). Hence for every v, φ(s)(x)(v) = η(y)(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) = η′(y)(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) = φ′(s)(x)(v), i.e. φ(s)(x) = φ′(s)(x) (extensionality of continuous alternating maps).
   (d) locality, applied with P := m, n := q, U := univ, T := X, ψ := φ(s), φ := φ′(s) and the open set N_s ⊇ spt X, gives X(φ(s)) = X(φ′(s)).
5. (Conclusion.) The functions s ↦ X(φ(s)) and s ↦ X(φ′(s)) agree on [0,1] = uIcc 0 1 (Set.uIcc_of_le), so intervalIntegral.integral_congr gives ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = ∫_0^1 X(φ′(s)) ds; no integrability is needed. By step 3, Z(η) = Z(η′). ∎

Then there is θ_s ∈ D^q(ℝ^m) such that (i) θ_s(x)(v) = θ(cons(s, x))(i ↦ ι(v_i)) for all x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, and (ii) θ_s(x) = ω(G_s(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G_s x) for every x ∈ ℝ^m with cons(s, x) ∈ N, where G_s := (fun x => G(cons(s, x))). For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1] ∧ tl(y) ∈ A}. For X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^q(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral).

Source: (Horizontal slices) and (Chain rule) in Part 0 of the supplied proof of dph_smooth_homotopy (4.1 of the source proof: j_s^#(G^#ω) = (G∘j_s)^#ω). Sibling used: compatible_form (iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm).

For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1] ∧ tl(y) ∈ A}. D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ. For X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^q(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral). j_s(x) := cons(s, x) and G_s := G∘j_s = (x ↦ G(cons(s, x))). For a q-covector α and a continuous linear map L, α.compContinuousLinearMap L is the covector v ↦ α(i ↦ L(v_i)) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply).

1. (The linear part ι.) Let ι : ℝ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ^{m+1} be the composition of the continuous linear map (0 : ℝ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ).finCons (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ) : ℝ^m →L[ℝ] (Fin (m+1) → ℝ), v ↦ Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ v), with the continuous linear equivalence (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm. By definition ι(v) = cons(0, v) for every v.
2. (Derivative of j_s.) For every x, HasFDerivAt j_s ι x: the map x ↦ Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x) has derivative (0).finCons (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ) at x (HasFDerivAt.finCons applied to hasFDerivAt_const s x and to the derivative of the continuous linear equivalence), and composing with the continuous linear equivalence (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (HasFDerivAt.comp) gives ι. Hence fderiv ℝ j_s x = ι for every x.
3. (j_s is a C^∞ isometry.) j_s(x) = ι(x) + j_s(0): after applying EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ both sides are (m+1)-tuples whose 0-th entries are s = 0 + s and whose (i+1)-th entries are x_i = x_i + 0 (case split with Fin.cases). Hence j_s is C^∞, as a continuous linear map plus a constant. Moreover ‖ι(v)‖ = ‖v‖, because ‖ι(v)‖² = 0² + Σ_i v_i² = ‖v‖² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Fin.sum_univ_succ). Therefore dist(j_s x, j_s x′) = ‖ι(x − x′)‖ = ‖x − x′‖, so j_s is an isometry (Isometry.of_dist_eq), hence a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding; ℝ^m is complete), and j_s⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.isCompact_preimage).
4. (The slice is a test form.) Apply compatible_form with P := m, Q := m+1, j := q, U := univ, V := univ, A := univ, f := j_s and the test form θ ∈ D^q(ℝ^{m+1}) = TestFormOn univ q. Its hypotheses hold: univ is open, A ⊆ U, j_s is C^∞ (step 3), and j_s⁻¹(K) ∩ univ is compact for every compact K (step 3). Source: Part 3 (Aff) of the supplied proof of dph_smooth_homotopy (Simon Ch. 6, 2.27: |h_#([[0,1]]×X)(ψ)| ≤ c·s·L^k·M(X)·sup|ψ|). The interior-product bound (F8) is the sibling interior_bound, whose constant is √(k+1), so here c := √(k+1); the supplied value c₁ = √(m′^k)·√m′ is not needed, since the statement only asks for some c ≥ 0 depending on (m, m′, k). Siblings used: mass_bound (cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le), compatible_form (iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm), slice_forms (iwl_cr_ci_slice_testForm), slice_comparison (dph_sh_apply_eq_of_eqOn_nhds_cyl) and interior_bound (dph_sh_covectorEuclideanNorm_interior_le).

Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p). For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1] ∧ tl(y) ∈ A}. D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ. For X ∈ D_q(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{q+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^q(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(cons(s, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m and v : Fin q → ℝ^m, one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral). As continuous linear maps: t : ℝ^{m+1} →L[ℝ] ℝ is (ContinuousLinearMap.proj 0) ∘ EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ; tl : ℝ^{m+1} →L[ℝ] ℝ^m is (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm ∘ (ContinuousLinearMap.pi (i ↦ proj i.succ)) ∘ EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ, whose middle factor is Fin.tail; and ι : ℝ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ^{m+1} is (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm ∘ ((0 : ℝ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ).finCons (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ)), so ι(v) = cons(0, v). The elementary identities t(cons(s, x)) = s, tl(cons(s, x)) = x, cons(t(y), tl(y)) = y, t(e₀) = 1, tl(e₀) = 0, t(ι v) = 0 and tl(ι v) = v follow from ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons and Fin.cons_self_tail (and EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 = (1, 0, …, 0)).

Fix m, m′, k and put c := √(k+1) ≥ 0. Let X, Z, F₀, F₁, O, s, L, B, ψ, C, η′ satisfy the hypotheses, let N′ be the open set ⊇ A := cyl(spt X) on which η′ = G^#ψ, and let G be the map of the statement.

1. (G is C^∞; its derivative.) G = F₀∘tl + t·(F₁∘tl − F₀∘tl). Since t and tl are continuous linear and F₀, F₁ are C^∞, G is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp, ContDiff.add, ContDiff.sub, ContDiff.smul). By the chain rule and the product rule for a scalar factor (HasFDerivAt.comp, HasFDerivAt.add, HasFDerivAt.sub, HasFDerivAt.smul), for every y and h:
   DG(y)h = DF₀(tl y)(tl h) + t(y)·(DF₁(tl y)(tl h) − DF₀(tl y)(tl h)) + t(h)·(F₁(tl y) − F₀(tl y)).
   In particular, for y = cons(s₀, x): DG(y)e₀ = F₁(x) − F₀(x), because tl(e₀) = 0 and t(e₀) = 1; and DG(y)(ι v) = DF₀(x)v + s₀·(DF₁(x)v − DF₀(x)v) = (1 − s₀)·DF₀(x)v + s₀·DF₁(x)v, because tl(ι v) = v and t(ι v) = 0.
2. (A is closed.) spt X = univ ∖ zeroRegion(X) is the complement of the open zero region (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion), so it is closed. Hence A = t⁻¹([0,1]) ∩ tl⁻¹(spt X) is closed.
3. (G is proper on A; (3a).) Let K ⊆ ℝ^{m′} be compact. K_s := cthickening s K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^{m′} is proper), so F₀⁻¹(K_s) ∩ spt X is compact by hypothesis, and so is its product with [0,1] and the image Q of that product under the continuous map (τ, x) ↦ cons(τ, x). Claim: G⁻¹(K) ∩ A ⊆ Q. Let y ∈ A with G(y) ∈ K, and put τ := t(y) ∈ [0,1] and x := tl(y) ∈ spt X ⊆ O. Then y = cons(τ, x), and dist(F₀(x), G(y)) = ‖τ·(F₁(x) − F₀(x))‖ = τ·dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ 1·s, so F₀(x) ∈ K_s (Metric.mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). The set G⁻¹(K) ∩ A is closed (G is continuous, K is closed, step 2), hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
4. (A compatible test form supported over O; (3b).) U := tl⁻¹(O) is open, and A ⊆ U because spt X ⊆ O. Apply compatible_form with P := m+1, Q := m′, j := k+1, this U, V := univ, A, f := G and ω := ψ; its properness hypothesis is step 3. We obtain η̂ ∈ TestFormOn U (k+1), ζ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ and an open N̂ with A ⊆ N̂, 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, η̂(y) = ζ(y)·ψ(G(y)).compContinuousLinearMap (DG(y)) for every y, and η̂(y) = ψ(G(y)).compContinuousLinearMap (DG(y)) for y ∈ N̂. Since η̂ is a test form with tsupport η̂ ⊆ U ⊆ univ, the same underlying form defines η̃ ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) = TestFormOn univ (k+1). Moreover η̃(y) = 0 whenever y ∉ U, because then y ∉ tsupport η̂ (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
5. (Replacing η′.) η′ and η̃ both equal G^#ψ on the open set N′ ∩ N̂ ⊇ A = cyl(spt X). By slice_comparison (with q := k), Z(η′) = Z(η̃).
6. (Slices.) slice_forms (P := m, m := k) applied to η̃ gives φ̂ : ℝ → D^k(ℝ^m) with φ̂(s₀)(x)(v) = η̃(cons(s₀, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i))) for all s₀, x, v. By ProdChar(X, Z), Z(η̃) = ∫_0^1 X(φ̂(s₀)) ds₀.
7. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ψ(0)| ≤ C.
8. (Pointwise bound; (3c).) Claim: |φ̂(s₀)(x)| ≤ c·s·L^k·C for every s₀ ∈ [0,1] and x ∈ ℝ^m. Put y := cons(s₀, x), so t(y) = s₀ and tl(y) = x.
   (a) If x ∉ O, then y ∉ U, so η̃(y) = 0 by step 4. Hence φ̂(s₀)(x)(v) = 0 for all v, i.e. φ̂(s₀)(x) = 0, and |0| = 0 ≤ c·s·L^k·C because all factors are ≥ 0 (step 7; covectorEuclideanNorm_zero).
   (b) If x ∈ O, let w := F₁(x) − F₀(x) and T := DG(y)∘ι : ℝ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ^{m′}. By step 1, DG(y)e₀ = w and T(v) = (1 − s₀)·DF₀(x)v + s₀·DF₁(x)v. For every v : Fin k → ℝ^m, step 4 and DG(y) ∘ Fin.cons e₀ (i ↦ ι(v_i)) = Fin.cons (DG(y)e₀) (i ↦ DG(y)(ι(v_i))) (Fin.comp_cons) give
   φ̂(s₀)(x)(v) = ζ(y)·ψ(G(y))(DG(y)e₀, DG(y)ι(v_1), …, DG(y)ι(v_k)) = ζ(y)·ψ(G(y))(Fin.cons w (i ↦ T(v_i))).
   So interior_bound, with γ := ψ(G(y)), a := ζ(y) and β := φ̂(s₀)(x), gives |φ̂(s₀)(x)| ≤ |ζ(y)|·√(k+1)·‖w‖·‖T‖^k·|ψ(G(y))|. Now |ζ(y)| ≤ 1; ‖w‖ = dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ s; ‖T‖ ≤ L by ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound, because ‖T(v)‖ ≤ (1 − s₀)·‖DF₀(x)‖·‖v‖ + s₀·‖DF₁(x)‖·‖v‖ ≤ ((1 − s₀)L + s₀L)‖v‖ = L‖v‖ (s₀ ∈ [0,1] and x ∈ O), hence ‖T‖^k ≤ L^k (pow_le_pow_left₀); and |ψ(G(y))| ≤ C. All factors are ≥ 0, so |φ̂(s₀)(x)| ≤ 1·√(k+1)·s·L^k·C = c·s·L^k·C.
9. (Mass bound; (3d).) For s₀ ∈ [0,1], mass_bound with P := m, n := k, U = W := univ, T := X, ω := φ̂(s₀), the bound B (0 ≤ B, and X.massOn univ = X.mass ≤ ofReal B by the definition of mass), tsupport φ̂(s₀) ⊆ univ and the pointwise bound of step 8 gives |X(φ̂(s₀))| ≤ B·(c·s·L^k·C).
